thread:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — competitor rolled out a "TileServe" style feature that stitches small capability tiles for routing. Do we treat as parity or build our own twist?
Alex Rivera: Saw it. Looks like a routing + light-model-composition layer. From infra side, main cost is more KV state + scheduling.
Tess Okafor: From UX this could be framed as "Composable Responses" vs "TileServe". We can keep simpler surfaces for 1.0.
Samir Patel: Sales already getting asks from midmarket customers asking for "matchmaker" behavior (route parts to different models). Acme pilot asked about it yesterday.
Rita Gomez: Technical note — we already have prefix-caching + routing policy primitives. Building a small composition layer might be doable as a 1-week spike. Quant/latency risk though.
Maya Chen: Proposal: 1) Do a 1-week technical spike to validate feasibility + perf (owner: Alex). 2) Define minimal parity spec (what customers expect) and a differentiator narrative (our cost-aware routing + rollout controls). 3) If spike ok, pilot with Acme as GTM anchor.
Alex Rivera: OK to spike. Plan: prototype a router that maps request segments to model tiles, implement KV checkpointing for tile state. Measure p95 and cost per 1k tokens.
Rita Gomez: For spike I'll run microbenchmarks on 1) quantized tile models 2) tiled kv cache size. Hypothesis: small tiles increase memory churn.
Noah Li: Deploy monitoring hooks please — add per-tile latency, cross-tile tail latency, and tile-fallback counts. I can wire into Console dashboards.
Maya Chen: Launch acceptance criteria (draft):
```
- P0: end-to-end p95 (user-visible) < 200ms for standard prompt mix
- P0: error rate < 1% and no regression in existing flows
- P1: cost delta <= +20% vs single-model baseline (unless explicit trade identified)
- P1: canary rollout plan: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on SLO breach
- P2: documented API surface with simple composition primitives and examples
```
Alex Rivera: Can we make the first canary run use routing-only (no model swaps) to validate routing infra?
Tess Okafor: UX note — keep the composition API as a declarative route table; avoid heavy client-side orchestration. Example snippet looks like: 
```
routes:
  - name: intent-detector
    model: small-intent-v1
    match: prefix: "intent:"
  - name: answer
    model: longform-v2
```
Samir Patel: I'll ask Acme for permission to be pilot. If accepted, we can use their use-case in marketing (with permission). Samir -> aim to close pilot yes/no by EOD Fri.
Rita Gomez: Risk log:
- Increased CPU/GPU scheduling overhead for many small loads
- KV cache spikes leading to OOM at tail
- Instrumentation gaps across tiles
I'll add mitigations in the spike doc.
Maya Chen: Decision: run spike next week. If spike passes perf + cost bar, product will fund a 6-sprint roadmap: M1 spike -> M2 internal pilot -> M3 customer pilot -> M4 API stable -> M5 GTM + docs -> M6 scaling/ops hardening.
Alex Rivera: I'll create the spike PR and attach perf harness. ETA for prototype logs: Wed EOD.
Noah Li: I'll pre-create dashboard and alerts so spike data is captured from day 1.
deploy-bot: New deploy scheduled: canary-infra-test -> staging at 4401234588 by alexr.
Maya Chen: Action items recap — Alex: spike + prototype (Wed EOD). Rita: perf benchmarks + mitigation list (Thu). Samir: pilot ask + permission (Fri EOD). Noah: dashboards/alerts (Mon). Tess: API UX proto + examples (Thu). I'll sync on Fri 10am to decide next step.
Alex Rivera: cool. Starting now.
Samir Patel: pinging Acme pm now.
Tess Okafor: mockups incoming in thread.
Maya Chen: Thanks all — aim for minimal parity with a clear replayable differentiator: cost-aware, per-route fallbacks, and rollout controls. :thumbsup:
